Patrick Henry Winston — How to Speak

harnessExplanation.role: The Laws tab (Tests.lawspec) says what must be true. Solution implements the function. Harness.lawspec describes how to choose inputs for the generated property checks.
harnessExplanation.declaration: The first line names this harness; for names the unit in Laws that it tests. A strategy is a generator: a recipe for drawing inputs. :: introduces its type, where limits its values and any requests generation. for law selects the claim by its full name; use supplies a strategy for one quantified input. A quantified input is a variable introduced by for all.
harnessExplanation.scope: A strategy changes the inputs sampled, not the requirement in Laws. A passing sample says only that the checks passed for the inputs tried. It is not a proof, and changing a generator to avoid a failure does not repair a bug or a false claim.
harnessExplanation.execution: The generated test runner is also called a harness. You edit the LawSpec configuration here; the compiler builds the runner that calls your implementation and records results. Run checks executes the set shown beneath the button: Examples + boundaries selects concrete and boundary checks; Sampled properties selects generated property cases; All checks includes both. Each step selects its teaching mode; Test controls also offers explicitly named alternate runs. Seed repeats generation under the same code, generator and tool versions; Replay failure also uses the recorded path to the failing case. F# runs through Fable and the JavaScript runner with fast-check in this browser, separately from native .NET/FsCheck.

namingGuide: English phrase names make claims and descriptive helpers readable. Write "|adding zero keeps the input| with no closing quote. Reuse the full delimited name in for law or a function call. Keep concise code names where they read naturally: add, sort, xs and numbers. Existing short names remain valid, including names in saved drafts.
